name: Speculative decoding drafter bottlenecks: draft LM-head projection and quantized drafter scaling
arithmetic_intensity: In modern auxiliary-head speculative drafters (EAGLE-3, Medusa, MTP), the drafter backbone is compact (1-2 layers, hidden size d), but its LM-head must project hidden states to the full target vocabulary V (e.g. V = 128k in Llama-3, V = 152k in Qwen3). Consequently, computing logits over V requires 2 * k * d * V FLOPs and streaming d * V weights from memory. As shown by Plaksin et al. (SlimSpec, arXiv:2605.10453), LM-head latency accounts for 45%-60% of total draft latency T_draft. Similarly, in full-model drafters, quantizing drafter weights to 4-bit (MXFP4 / ML-SpecQD, arXiv:2503.13565) halves draft memory traffic and accelerates drafting in memory-bound regimes.
scales_with: drafter_rank_r (rank of factorized LM projection in low-rank heads)
batch_size (at batch >= 32-64, LM-head GEMM becomes compute-bound)

hardware_parameters.effect: Governs drafter LM-head weight streaming latency at low batch sizes (batch 1-16).

workarounds: Low-rank drafter LM-head (SlimSpec): factorize projection d x V into d x r and r x V (e.g. r = d/8), reducing LM-head latency by 2-3x while preserving full vocabulary support
Quantized drafts (ML-SpecQD): direct-cast 4-bit (MXFP4) quantization of draft weights to reduce memory footprint and latency in client/edge inference
Static vocabulary truncation (VocabTrim, FR-Spec): limit drafter predictions to top 32k-64k frequent tokens, cutting LM-head work at the cost of capping maximum acceptance rate
Clustered / dynamic vocabulary routing (SpecVocab, DynaSpec): dynamically route contexts to token clusters
notes: Quantized drafters and draft-head optimization represent the current generation of speculative decoding engineering. When the drafter backbone is reduced to a single transformer layer or feature head, the LM-head projection (which cannot be easily pruned without hurting rare tokens) emerges as the dominant computational and bandwidth bottleneck of the drafting phase.
